guard_streams.write_limit: Crowdsourced mobile-device observations describe mobile experience in sampled coverage areas and cannot establish fixed-broadband parcel coverage or measured fixed speed.

facts.detail: The 2025 Mobile Matters report was published on 17 July 2025.
The crowdsourced dataset covers October 2024 to March 2025.
The research used crowdsourced mobile-device data supplied by Opensignal.
Seventy-one percent of observed cellular data connections used 4G.
Twenty-eight percent used 5G.
Observed connections included 0.7 percent on 3G and 0.2 percent on 2G.
5G represented 29 percent of urban connections and 19 percent of rural connections.
A 2 MB download averaged 0.3 seconds on 5G, 0.7 on 4G and 4.9 on 3G.
The report analyses connection rates, file transfers, response times and speed distributions.
Results are broken down by mobile network operator and location.

guard_streams.write_limit: Affordability research describes household experience, survey responses and social-tariff awareness; it is not physical network availability or parcel performance evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom first published the tracker page on 27 February 2024.
The page was last updated on 14 May 2026.
The tracker covers home broadband, mobile, landline and pay-TV affordability.
Ofcom uses the tracker to monitor people's experience of communications-service affordability.
The latest page includes an April 2026 chart series.
Financial vulnerability combines household income, work status and household size.
In October 2025, 36 percent did not know or declined to answer the household-income question.
The page links an October 2025 technical annex.
Underlying data is made available through Ofcom's statistical release calendars.
Previous releases include Q3 and Q1 2025 data tables, codebooks and SPSS files.

guard_streams.source: Report: Complaints about broadband, landline, mobile and pay-TV services
guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint rates measure customer dissatisfaction relative to provider subscriber bases and cannot establish coverage, orderability or parcel-measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom first published the complaints report page on 25 January 2024.
The page was updated on 23 July 2026.
It covers landline, fixed broadband, pay-monthly mobile and pay-TV complaints.
Provider comparisons use complaints per 100,000 customers.
The latest trends cover January to March 2026.
Overall complaints decreased compared with Q4 2025.
Fixed-broadband complaints decreased.
Pay-monthly mobile complaints decreased.
Landline complaints stayed at the same level.
Pay-TV complaints stayed at the same level.
